answer:
**Adding GPUs can change the training algorithm even when the code barely changes.** If each of eight GPUs keeps the old local batch size, global batch grows eightfold. There are then fewer optimizer updates per epoch, different gradient noise, and potentially a mismatched learning-rate schedule. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/index.html)

**Compare the budgets explicitly.** A dataset of 8,000 examples with batch 100 gives 80 updates per epoch on one GPU. Eight replicas each processing 100 examples give global batch 800 and only ten synchronized updates per epoch. Training for the same number of epochs is not training for the same number of updates.

Check whether the intended experiment kept global batch fixed or increased it. Adjust rate, warmup, scheduler units, and training duration based on that choice rather than automatically applying one scaling rule. Verify that distributed sampling partitions data correctly and reshuffles across epochs.

BatchNorm may use local per-rank statistics unless synchronized; changing local batch size can therefore change the forward model. Gradient accumulation, loss averaging, and unequal final batches can also introduce scaling errors.

Before tuning away a three-point drop, compare a deterministic small distributed run with an equivalent single-device update under compatible conditions. Confirm data coverage, gradient scaling, and checkpoint evaluation. Only then investigate the statistical effects of the larger global batch or altered normalization.

**Technical details and references.**

With per-device batch unchanged, eight-way DDP increases the global batch eightfold and reduces optimizer updates per epoch by roughly eightfold. The same epoch count and learning-rate schedule therefore describe a different optimization process. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/index.html) [2](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)

Check global batch including accumulation, learning-rate/warmup tuning, scheduler units, gradient averaging versus summation, and whether the distributed sampler changes shuffle each epoch. Ensure evaluation aggregates all examples without accidental duplicates or dropped tails. BatchNorm uses local statistics unless synchronized; its effective normalization batch may differ from the global optimization batch.

Compare first with a configuration preserving the original global batch and update count. Then change batch size deliberately and retune. There is no single setting guaranteed to recover exactly the missing three percentage points.
